nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الۤر تِلْكَ آيَاتُ ٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿الۤر﴾: he said: [It means] "I am Allah; I see."
Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us; he said: al-Zaʿfarānī narrated to us; he said: ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd narrated to us; he said: Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿الۤر﴾ — he said: I am Allah; I see.
And in the narration of ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿الر﴾, ﴿حم﴾ and ﴿ن﴾ are the letters of «الرحمن» (al-Raḥmān), separated.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have explained this at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
The meaning of ﴿ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾ according to the people of language is «المُحْكَم» (made firm), just as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿هَذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾, that is, «مُعَدٌّ» (prepared) [Translator's note: a faʿīl pattern in the sense of a passive participle].

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾.
It is narrated that by "the people" here is meant the people of Mecca, because they said: How strange! Did Allah find no messenger other than Abū Ṭālib's orphan? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿أَكَانَ لِلنَّاسِ عَجَباً أَنْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰ رَجُلٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَنْ أَنذِرِ ٱلنَّاسَ﴾.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, an abode of truth.
And it was said: «القَدَم» is righteous deeds.
And it was said: precedence (al-sābiqa).
And it is narrated from al-Ḥasan or Qatāda that he said: «القَدَم» is Muḥammad ﷺ, who intercedes for them.
Abū Zayd said: «رجلٌ قَدَمٌ», that is, a brave man.
Qatāda said: That is, a forerunner of truth.
Mujāhid said: That is, [a forerunner] of good.
And in the narration of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa from him [Ibn ʿAbbās], he said: Happiness was decreed for them beforehand in the first record.
These views are close to one another, and the meaning is: a lofty rank.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ﴾.
There had been no mention of an intercessor [before this], because the meaning was already known, since they used to say: "These are our intercessors with Allah." Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَا مِن شَفِيعٍ إِلاَّ مِن بَعْدِ إِذْنِهِ﴾, that is, no intercessor intercedes except for one whom He has approved.

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقّاً إِنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar "Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ" read: ﴿أَنَّهُ يَبْدَأُ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ﴾ [with fatḥa on the hamza].
Abū Jaʿfar [al-Naḥḥās] said: Reading it with fatḥa admits two meanings:
One of them: "because He…".
The other: "the promise of Allah that He…".
And «القسط» is justice.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ ٱلشَّمْسَ ضِيَآءً وَٱلْقَمَرَ نُوراً وَقَدَّرَهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾.
He did not say «وقدَّرهما» (and He measured them both), because what is measured out for the number of years and the reckoning is the moon.
And it [has] twenty-eight stations.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: It is possible that the meaning is «وقدَّرهما», and then [one of them] was omitted, as [the poet] said:
نَحْنُ بِمَا عِنْدَنَا وَأَنْتَ بِمَا * عِنْدَكَ رَاضٍ، والرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We are content with what we have, and you with what you have — and opinion differs.) [i.e. "content" is stated once for both.]

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ يَهْدِيهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِإِيمَانِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, He makes for them a light by which they walk.
And there is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ what strengthens this, that he said: "The believer is met by his deed in the most beautiful form, and it keeps him company and guides him; and the disbeliever is met by his deed in the ugliest form, and it frightens him and leads him astray." This is the sense of the ḥadīth.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿دَعْوَاهُمْ فِيهَا سُبْحَانَكَ ٱللَّهُمَّ﴾.
That is: their supplication is declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, free of imperfection. ﴿وَتَحِيَّتُهُمْ فِيهَا سَلاَمٌ﴾: that is, they greet one another with [wishes of] safety.
And it is possible that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, greets them with peace, as an honour to them.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
So He informed that the opening of their supplication is declaring Allah free of imperfection, and its end is thanking Him.

nahhas-meani:11-11.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ يُعَجِّلُ ٱللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ ٱلشَّرَّ ٱسْتِعْجَالَهُمْ بِٱلْخَيْرِ لَقُضِيَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَجَلُهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It is a man's supplicating, when angry, against his family and his children; if that were hastened for them, they would die.
And it was said: It is their saying ﴿اللَّهُمَّ إنْ كَانَ هَذَا هُوَ الحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدَكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ﴾.
If this were hastened for them, they would perish.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ ٱلضُّرُّ دَعَانَا لِجَنبِهِ أَوْ قَاعِداً أَوْ قَآئِماً﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and when harm touches man while lying down, or sitting, or standing, he calls upon Us.
And it is possible that the implied construction (taqdīr) is: he calls upon Us in one of these states.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلَمَّا كَشَفْنَا عَنْهُ ضُرَّهُ مَرَّ كَأَن لَّمْ يَدْعُنَآ إِلَىٰ ضُرٍّ مَّسَّهُ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayd narrated from Abū ʿUbayda that «مرَّ» is in the sense of «استمرَّ» (he continued).
Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, he continued in what he had been upon before the harm touched him.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَا ٱلْقُرُونَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُواْ وَجَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ﴾.
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ — there are two views on it:
One of them: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed of what He knew of them had He let them remain.
The other: that He requited them for their disbelief by sealing their hearts.
And what indicates this is that He said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ نَجْزِي ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَرْجُونَ لِقَآءَنَا ٱئْتِ بِقُرْآنٍ غَيْرِ هَـٰذَآ أَوْ بَدِّلْهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: Those who said this were the idolaters of the people of Mecca.
Someone else said: That is, bring a Qurʾān in which there is no mention of the resurrection and the raising, nor insulting of our gods. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ مَا يَكُونُ لِيۤ أَنْ أُبَدِّلَهُ مِن تِلْقَآءِ نَفْسِيۤ﴾.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿قُل لَّوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا تَلَوْتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَلاَ أَدْرَاكُمْ بِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, nor would He have made you aware of it, nor informed you of it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَقَدْ لَبِثْتُ فِيكُمْ عُمُراً مِّن قَبْلِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: He remained among them forty years, and he spent two years seeing the visions of the prophets; and he ﷺ died at the age of sixty-two.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ﴾ [verse 18].
That is: what does not harm them if they do not worship it, nor benefit them if they worship it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ شُفَعَاؤُنَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ قُلْ أَتُنَبِّئُونَ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا لاَ يَعْلَمُ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
That is: Do you worship what does not intercede, nor help, nor discern, and say: It intercedes for us with Allah — and so you lie? And is it possible for you to inform Him of what He does not know?

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ إِلاَّ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَٱخْتَلَفُواْ﴾.
There are three views on it:
The clearest of them is the view of Mujāhid: that in the time of Adam ﷺ they were upon a single religion, then they differed.
The second view: that this is general [in wording] with a specific meaning, and that "the people" here means the Arabs specifically.
The third view: that it is like his saying ﷺ: "Every child is born upon the natural disposition (al-fiṭra)", that is, then they differ after that.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَآ أَذَقْنَا ٱلنَّاسَ رَحْمَةً مِّن بَعْدِ ضَرَّآءَ مَسَّتْهُمْ﴾.
By "the people" here the disbelievers are meant, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿إنَّ الإِنْسَانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is the hypocrite.
The mercy here is relief, and ﴿مِّن بَعْدِ ضَرَّآءَ﴾ means: after distress.
﴿إِذَا لَهُمْ مَّكْرٌ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا﴾: that is, they use stratagems so as to attribute the cause of the mercy to something other than its [true] source.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إِذَا لَهُمْ مَّكْرٌ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا﴾: mockery and denial.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾.
It was said: The meaning is "until, when you are in the ships"; then the address was turned to the Prophet ﷺ, so the meaning became: "and they sailed with them, O Muḥammad."
And it was said: The Arabs put the absent in the place of the present and address him as such, then return him to the absent [person] (iltifāt).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ أُحِيطَ بِهِمْ﴾.
It is said of one who has fallen into a calamity: «قد أُحيط به» (he has been surrounded), as though the calamity has encompassed him. The origin of this is that when the enemy surrounds a place, its people have perished.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا هُمْ يَبْغُونَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ ٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
«البغي» is tending towards corruption. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is said: «بغى الجرحُ يبغِي بغياً» when a wound tends towards festering.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّمَا بَغْيُكُمْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِكُمْ﴾.
That is: your working of injustice comes back upon you.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿مَّتَاعَ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
That is: whatever you obtain through transgression and corruption is only something you take pleasure in during this world. This is the view of the people of language.
It is narrated from Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna that he said: "He meant that transgression is an enjoyment of the life of this world, that is, its punishment is hastened for the one who does it in this world."
As it is said: "Transgression is a place of downfall." And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنْصُرَنَّهُ اللهُ﴾.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَا مَثَلُ ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا كَمَآءٍ أَنزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَٱخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ ٱلأَرْضِ مِمَّا يَأْكُلُ ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلأَنْعَامُ﴾. «[Translator's note: the quotation in the source begins «مَا مَثَلُ» for «إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ».]»
The vegetation mingled with the rain, and the rain with the vegetation.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَخَذَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ زُخْرُفَهَا﴾.
«الزخرف» in the language is perfection of beauty; and from it gold was called «زُخْرُف».
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿كَأَن لَّمْ تَغْنَ بِٱلأَمْسِ﴾.
That is: as though it had not flourished.
And the meaning according to the people of language is: as though it had not been inhabited.
And «المعاني» are the dwellings that people inhabit; and «غَنيتُ بالمنزلِ» means: I resided in the dwelling and inhabited it. «[Translator's note: «المعاني» here is evidently a misprint for «المغاني» (dwellings), from the same root as تَغْنَ.]» «[Translator's note: «كأنْ تَنْعم» in the source presumably stands for «كأنْ لم تَنْعم»; translated in that sense.]»

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ يَدْعُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ دَارِ ٱلسَّلاَمِ﴾.
Qatāda said: «دار السلام» is Paradise, and «السلام» is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning on this [view] is: and Allah invites to His abode.
And repeating the noun [instead of a pronoun], when it is not ambiguous, is more majestic.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: And it is possible that the meaning is — and Allah knows best — He invites to the abode in which one is safe from afflictions.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the people of ḥadīth hold is that «الحُسنى» is Paradise and the "increase" is looking upon Allah, exalted be His name. Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar narrated to us; he said: Hannād narrated to us; he said: Wakīʿ narrated to us, from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, from Abū Tamīma al-Hujaymī, from Abū Mūsā, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾: he said: Paradise; ﴿وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾: he said: looking upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Al-Ḥusayn narrated to us; he said: Hannād narrated to us; he said: Qabīṣa narrated to us; he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us; — and it was read to Ibn Bint Manīʿ, from Hudba ibn Khālid; he said: Ḥammād ibn Salama narrated to us — from Thābit al-Bunānī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, from Ṣuhayb; he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited ﴿لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ وَزِيَادَةٌ﴾ and said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with Allah which He wishes to fulfil for you. They will say: And what is it? Has Allah not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us to Paradise and saved us from the Fire? Then the veil will be lifted and He will manifest Himself, and they will look at Him, Mighty and Majestic is He." He said: By Allah, Allah has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him, and that is the "increase".
Abū Jaʿfar said: In the ḥadīth of Ibn Bint Manīʿ [it has] "and let us pass (wa-yujiznā)", and in his ḥadīth [it has] "and they will look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He".
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلاَ ذِلَّةٌ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: «القَتَر» is blackness of the faces.
Someone else said: «القَتَر» is the plural of «قَتَرة», which is dust.
The meaning of ﴿يَرْهَقُ﴾ is: covers; and «الذلّة» is abasement.
In the ḥadīth of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā: ﴿وَلاَ يَرْهَقُ وُجُوهَهُمْ قَتَرٌ وَلاَ ذِلَّةٌ﴾ — he said: after their looking at their Lord.
And «العاصم» is the one who protects.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا أُغْشِيَتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ قِطَعاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ مُظْلِماً﴾.
«القِطَع» is the plural of «قِطْعة»; and whoever read ﴿قِطْعاً﴾, it is the name of what is cut off. It is said: «قَطَعَهُ قَطْعاً», and the name of what you have cut off is «قِطْعٌ». «[Translator's note: the source prints the last word as «قِطَعٌ»; the argument requires «قِطْعٌ».]»

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ نَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ مَكَانَكُمْ﴾.
That is: wait in your place — a threat.
﴿فَزَيَّلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ is from your saying «زِلتُ الشيءَ من الشيءِ», that is, I removed it; and «زَيَّلْتُ» is for intensification.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ شَهِيداً بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾.
Because they said: Who bears witness for you that you are the Messenger of Allah?

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُنَالِكَ تَبْلُواْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَّآ أَسْلَفَتْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, it tests.
And its meaning is: it finds it and comes to know it.
And concerning ﴿تَبْلُواْ﴾ there are two views: «[Translator's note: the two views that follow concern the variant reading «تَتْلُو»; the source prints «تَبْلُوا» here.]»
Al-Akhfash said: That is, it reads, as He said: ﴿وكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ ألْزَمْنَاه طَائِرهُ في عُنُقِهِ ونُخْرِجُ لَهُ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ كِتَاباً يَلْقَاهُ مَنْشُوراً. اقرَأْ كِتَابَكَ﴾.
The other view: that the meaning of ﴿تَبْلُواْ﴾ is "it follows", as [the poet] said:
* قَدْ جَعَلْتَ دَلْوِي تَسْتَتْلِيني *
(My bucket has begun to make me follow it.)

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ فَسَقُوۤاْ﴾.
Then He explained "the word" and said: ﴿أَنَّهُمْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾. So the meaning is: it has become due against them that they will not believe [Translator's note: the anna-clause being a badal (substitute) for "the word"].
And it is possible that the meaning is: because they do not believe, and "the word" would be the punishment.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ أَن يُفْتَرَىٰ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Its meaning is: «لأنْ يُفترى» (to be forged), that is, to be fabricated.
And it is possible that the meaning of ﴿وَمَا كَانَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ أَن يُفْتَرَىٰ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is as you say: "This Qurʾān was not a lie" [Translator's note: the interpreted maṣdar being the khabar of kāna].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن تَصْدِيقَ ٱلَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: but the confirmation of the thing before which the Qurʾān is [i.e. that preceded it], that is, it confirms the scriptures and the reports of the nations that preceded it.
And it is possible that the meaning is: that it confirms what has not yet come of the matter of the Hour.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْ يَقُولُونَ ٱفْتَرَاهُ قُلْ فَأْتُواْ بِسُورَةٍ مِّثْلِهِ﴾.
The meaning is: a sūra like its sūras, as in ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ [Translator's note: with a muḍāf omitted], the genus being meant.
And it was said: The meaning is: then bring a Qurʾān like this Qurʾān; and a sūra is Qurʾān, so He referred to it with the masculine [pronoun] according to the meaning; had it been according to the wording it would have been said «مثلِها».
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱدْعُواْ مَنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
That is: call whoever will help you, of those who follow your way, ﴿إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ that it is forged.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يُحِيطُواْ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾.
It was said: By this is meant — and Allah knows best — whoever denies while in doubt.
And it was said: ﴿بِمَا لَمْ يُحِيطُواْ بِعِلْمِهِ﴾, that is, the threat it contains for their disbelief.
﴿وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾: that is, what that threat leads to.
And it was said: ﴿وَلَمَّا يَأْتِهِمْ تَأْوِيلُهُ﴾, that is, they have not understood it; and this indicates that it is obligatory to look into interpretation.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and there has not yet come to them the punishment to which their affair leads.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن لاَّ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ وَرَبُّكَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾.
That is: among them is he who knows that it is true but displays disbelief out of obstinacy and to preserve his leadership, ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن لاَّ يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾ in secret or in public.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُونَ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنتَ تُسْمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ..؟﴾.
That is: their outward appearance is the appearance of people who listen, but because of the intensity of their enmity and their turning away from the Prophet ﷺ they are in the position of the deaf.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانُواْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
That is: even if, along with this, they are ignorant?!

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ أَفَأَنْتَ تَهْدِي ٱلْعُمْيَ وَلَوْ كَانُواْ لاَ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾.
﴿وَمِنهُمْ مَّن يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ﴾: that is, he keeps looking at you, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ إلَيْكَ تَدُورُ أعْيُنُهُمْ كَالَّذِي يُغْشَى عَلَيْهِ مِنَ المَوْتِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ كَأَن لَّمْ يَلْبَثُوۤاْ إِلاَّ سَاعَةً مِّنَ ٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
That is: what lies between their death and their resurrection is short. Then He said: ﴿يَتَعَارَفُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, that is, they recognise one another; and that is more severe for their rebuke, when they recognise one another [as partners] in misleading and corruption.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, whether We show you the punishment in your lifetime ﴿أَوْ نَتَوَفَّيَنَّكَ﴾ before that, ﴿فَإِلَيْنَا مَرْجِعُهُمْ﴾.
[Someone else said: By His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He,] ﴿وَإِمَّا نُرِيَنَّكَ بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِي نَعِدُهُمْ﴾ He means the battle of Badr. And Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَّسُولٌ فَإِذَا جَآءَ رَسُولُهُمْ قُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِٱلْقِسْطِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Day of Resurrection.
The meaning on this [view] is: when their messenger comes bearing witness against them as to belief and disbelief, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَكَيْفَ إذَا جِئنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ﴾?
And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَقَالَ الر‍َّسُولُ يَا رَبِّ إنَّ قَوْمِي اتَّخَذُوا هَذَا القُرْآنَ مَهْجُوراً﴾.
Someone other than Mujāhid said: It is possible [that the meaning is] that He does not punish anyone until the removal of excuse and the warning have come to him, and only the messengers bring this.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ بَيَاتاً أَوْ نَهَاراً مَّاذَا يَسْتَعْجِلُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: what do they hasten of Allah [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun refers to Allah].
And it is possible [that it is]: what of the punishment do the criminals hasten.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is closer to the meaning, because of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أَثُمَّ إذَا مَا وَقَعَ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ﴾?

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿الآنَ وَقَدْ كُنتُم بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾.
In the speech there is an omission, and the meaning is: Now you believe in it?

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَسْتَنْبِئُونَكَ أَحَقٌّ هُوَ﴾.
The meaning is: and they ask you for information, saying: Is it true?
﴿قُلْ إِي وَرَبِّيۤ إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ﴾: that is, the meaning [of إِي] is "yes".
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾.
That is: you are not among those who can escape being requited for their disbelief.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that the chiefs who called to disbelief concealed their regret when they saw the punishment.
The other: that ﴿أَسَرُّواْ﴾ means "they showed".
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: If this is correct, then its meaning is: regret appeared in the lines (asirra) of their faces; its singular is «سِرار», and they are the lines in the forehead.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدْ جَآءَتْكُمْ مَّوْعِظَةٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
He means the Qurʾān.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: His bounty is Islam, and His mercy is the Qurʾān.
Abū al-Tayyāḥ said: ﴿بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means Islam, ﴿وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ means the Qurʾān, ﴿فَبِذَلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُواْ﴾ O Companions of Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾ — he said: meaning the disbelievers.
ʿIkrima narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is the Qurʾān, ﴿وَبِرَحْمَتِهِ﴾ is that He made us among its people.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ مِّن رِّزْقٍ فَجَعَلْتُمْ مِّنْهُ حَرَاماً وَحَلاَلاً﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the baḥīras and the sāʾibas [animals the pagans dedicated and forbade].
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means [what is in] His saying ﴿وَجَعَلُوا للهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ الحَرْثِ وَالأَنْعَامِ نَصِيباً﴾.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ وَمَا تَتْلُواْ مِنْهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ وَلاَ تَعْمَلُونَ مِنْ عَمَلٍ إِلاَّ كُنَّا عَلَيْكُمْ شُهُوداً إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾.
The meaning of ﴿وَمَا تَكُونُ فِي شَأْنٍ﴾ is: whatever time you are engaged in an affair, of worship or otherwise. ﴿وَمَا تَتْلُواْ مِنْهُ مِن قُرْآنٍ﴾: Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning is: from the affair [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun in مِنْهُ refers to «الشأن»].
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذْ تُفِيضُونَ فِيهِ﴾.
That is: you engage in it; and from it is «أَفَاضَ في الحديث» (he launched into the talk).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَعْزُبُ عَن رَّبِّكَ مِن مِّثْقَالِ ذَرَّةٍ﴾.
That is: nothing is far or absent [from Him].
«مثقال الشيء» is its weight, and «الذرّة» is the small ant.

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّ أَوْلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾.
It is narrated that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: Who are the friends (awliyāʾ) of Allah? He said: "Those who, when they are seen, Allah is remembered."
"Abū Jaʿfar narrated to us; he said: al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUmar al-Kūfī narrated to us in Baghdad; he said: al-ʿAlāʾ ibn ʿAmr narrated to us; he said: Yaḥyā ibn al-Yamān narrated to us, from Ashʿath ibn Isḥāq al-Qummī, from Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿أَلاۤ إِنَّ أَوْلِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ لاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ — he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is remembered at the sight of them."

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿لَهُمُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ فِي ٱلْحَياةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِي ٱلآخِرَةِ﴾, and he said: "It is the righteous dream which the Muslim sees, or which is seen for him; and in the Hereafter: Paradise."
There is another view on it, which Shuʿba narrated from Ibn ʿImrān al-Jawnī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣāmit, from Abū Dharr: I said to the Prophet ﷺ: "A man does a good deed for himself, and people love him for it. He said: That is the believers' glad tidings hastened in this world." «[Translator's note: the narrator is usually named Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī; the source has «ابن عمران».]»
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: there is no breaking of His promise.
And it was said: The meaning of ﴿لاَ تَبْدِيلَ لِكَلِمَاتِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is: there is no changing His reports, that is, nothing abrogates them, and they will only be as He said.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ﴾.
That is: let not their threats, their denial and their arrogance towards you grieve you.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلْعِزَّةَ للَّهِ جَمِيعاً﴾.
That is: dominance belongs to Allah.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا يَتَّبِعُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلاَّ يَخْرُصُونَ﴾.
That is: they guess and conjecture.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْلَّيْلَ لِتَسْكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَٱلنَّهَارَ مُبْصِراً﴾.
That is: [a day] in which one sees, by way of attribution (ʿalā al-nasab), as He said: ﴿فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾, that is, possessing contentment, that is, one is content with it.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنْ عِندَكُمْ مِّن سُلْطَانٍ بِهَـٰذَآ﴾.
That is: you have no proof for this.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ لاَ يُفْلِحُونَ﴾.
The statement is complete [here].
Then He said: ﴿مَتَاعٌ فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾, that is: that is an enjoyment in this world [Translator's note: مَتَاعٌ being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ].

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُوۤاْ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَآءَكُمْ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: Its meaning is: and call your partners. He said: «الإجماع» is preparing and resolving upon a matter.
Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: It is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning of «أَجْمِعُوا» and «اجْمَعُوا» is one.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: The meaning is: together with your partners [Translator's note: i.e. a wāw of accompaniment, شركاءكم being mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment)]. He said: Al-Farrāʾ's view has no sense, because if he holds that the meaning is "and call your partners to help you", then its meaning is the meaning of «مع» (with); and if he holds it is calling only, then there is no sense in calling them for nothing.
Al-Jaḥdarī read — and it is also narrated from al-Aʿraj — ﴿فَاجْمَعُوا أمْرَكُمْ﴾ with a connecting alif and fatḥa on the mīm.
Al-Ḥasan read: ﴿فَأَجْمِعُوۤاْ أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاؤُكُمْ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This indicates that they are two dialectal forms with one meaning.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لاَ يَكُنْ أَمْرُكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ غُمَّةً﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that the meaning of «غُمَّة» is like the meaning of «غَمّ» (grief).
The other — and it is sounder linguistically — is that the meaning is: let your affair be manifest. It is said: «القومُ في غُمَّة» when their affair is obscure to them and confused; and from this is «غُمَّ الهلالُ على الناس», that is, something covered it and concealed it.
And «الغَمّ» (grief) from this is only the distress that covers the heart and constricts it; and the origin of this is derived from «الغَمامة» (the cloud).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ ٱقْضُوۤاْ إِلَيَّ وَلاَ تُنظِرُونَ﴾.
That is: then do whatever seems good to you.
Al-Kisāʾī said: And it is read ﴿وأفْضُوا إلَيَّ﴾ with a disjunctive alif (hamzat qaṭʿ) and with fāʾ.

nahhas-meani:78-78.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ أَجِئْتَنَا لِتَلْفِتَنَا عَمَّا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, to twist us away.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is well known in the language. It is said: «لَفَتَهُ يَلْفِتُه» when he turned him aside. And from this is «التفت» (he turned round): it is only turning aside from the direction in front of him.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَتَكُونَ لَكُمَا ٱلْكِبْرِيَآءُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, sovereignty; and that is well known in the language. Sovereignty was called «كبرياء» (grandeur) only because it is the greatest thing attained in this world.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَلْقُواْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ مَا جِئْتُمْ بِهِ ٱلسِّحْرُ﴾.
Whoever read ﴿آلسِّحْرُ﴾, its meaning for him is rebuke, that is: What is it that you have brought — is it magic?

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَآ آمَنَ لِمُوسَىٰ إِلاَّ ذُرِّيَّةٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, a few.
Mujāhid said: He means that none of them [the elders] believed in him; only their children believed.
Some of the people of language said: They were called "offspring" only because their fathers were Copts and their mothers were from the Children of Israel, just as those [of Persian descent] who ended up in Yemen from Persia were called "al-Abnāʾ" (the sons); he takes them to be men who are [specifically] referred to [by this name].
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿عَلَىٰ خَوْفٍ مِّن فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ أَن يَفْتِنَهُمْ﴾.
He said «ومَلَئِهِمْ» (and their chiefs) [with a plural pronoun] because it is known that with him were those who obeyed his orders and referred to his word.
And it was said: The meaning is: in fear of the family of Pharaoh.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا لاَ تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ. وَنَجِّنَا بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, do not destroy us at the hands of our enemies, nor punish us with a punishment from You, so that our enemies would say: Had they been in the right, we would not have been given power over them and they would not have been punished — that is, so that they would be tempted [further] by that.
Abū Mijlaz said: [That is,] let them not prevail and so think that they are better than us.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱجْعَلُواْ بُيُوتَكُمْ قِبْلَةً﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: That is, places of prayer.
Mujāhid said: That is, facing the Kaʿba.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: They were in fear, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed, so they were commanded to pray in their houses so that no harm would reach them.

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ آتَيْتَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلأَهُ زِينَةً وَأَمْوَالاً فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَ﴾. «وَلِيُضِلُّوا».
The meaning is: so that brought them to misguidance, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنُ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوّاً وَحَزَناً﴾, that is: their affair ended up in that, and it is as though they did that for this [purpose].
Some of the people of language say: [It is] the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), and it is in reality the lām of «كي» (purpose).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿رَبَّنَا ٱطْمِسْ عَلَىٰ أَمْوَالِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: It has reached us that their wealth and their crops became stones.
Mujāhid said: That is, destroy it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the language to say «طَمَسَ الموضعُ» when a place is effaced and obliterated.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱشْدُدْ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, with misguidance.
Someone else said: That is, harden them.
And the meaning is one.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ يُؤْمِنُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَرَوُاْ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلأَلِيمَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He [Moses] supplicated against them.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is because when they see the punishment, belief will not benefit them; so he supplicated against them.
Abū Isḥāq said: Abū al-ʿAbbās said: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His saying ﴿رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِكَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَّعْوَتُكُمَا فَٱسْتَقِيمَا﴾.
Qatāda said: Moses supplicated and Aaron said "Āmīn".
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Samāʿa narrated to us in Kufa; he said: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us; he said: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī narrated to us, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliya; he said: ﴿قَدْ أُجِيبَتْ دَّعْوَتُكُمَا﴾ — he said: Moses supplicated and Aaron said "Āmīn", may Allah bless them both.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is good according to the people of language, because saying "Āmīn" is a supplication. Do you not see that the meaning of «آمين» is "answer [us]"?

nahhas-meani:90-90.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَاوَزْنَا بِبَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَتْبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُ بَغْياً وَعَدْواً﴾.
Qatāda read: ﴿فاتَّبَعَهُمْ فِرْعَوْنُ وَجُنُودُهُ﴾ with a connecting alif.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: It is said «أتْبَعَهُ», with a disjunctive alif, when he caught up with him and reached him; and «اتَّبَعَهُ», with a connecting alif, when he followed his tracks, whether he reached him or not. Abū Zayd said likewise.
And it was said: «اتَّبعه» with a connecting alif [is used] in a matter: he took him as a model; and «أتْبَعَهُ» with a disjunctive alif [is used] for good or evil. This is the view of Abū ʿAmr.
And it was said: They are one.
Qatāda read: ﴿بَغْياً وَعُدُوًّا﴾, and «العُدُوّ» is injustice.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَآ أَدْرَكَهُ ٱلْغَرَقُ قَالَ آمَنتُ أَنَّهُ لاۤ إِلِـٰهَ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِي آمَنَتْ بِهِ بَنوۤاْ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾.
Shuʿba narrated from ʿAdī ibn Thābit and ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib; they said: We heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrating from Ibn ʿAbbās — Shuʿba said: one of the two traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ — he said: "Gabriel, peace be upon him, was stuffing mud and putting it into Pharaoh's mouth," he said, "for fear that he would say: There is no god but You, and He would forgive him."
ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: It has reached me that Gabriel said to the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Iblīs never begot a child more hateful to me than Pharaoh. When drowning overtook him he said ﴿آمَنْتُ﴾ — the verse — and I feared he would say it and be shown mercy, so I took some earth, or some mud, and stuffed it into his mouth."
And it was said: Gabriel did this to him only as a punishment for the enormity of what he used to commit.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱلْيَوْمَ نُنَجِّيكَ بِبَدَنِكَ لِتَكُونَ لِمَنْ خَلْفَكَ آيَةً﴾.
Qatāda said: A group of people did not believe that he had drowned, so he was brought out to be an admonition and a sign.
Someone else said: The sign in it is that he claimed to be a lord and his people used to worship him, so Allah showed him to them after He had drowned him.
And part of the sign in it is that he drowned together with his people, and he was brought out without them.
Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning of ﴿نُنَجِّيكَ﴾ is: We cast you onto a height (najwa) of the land.
Someone else said: «النَّجْوة» and «النَّبْوة» are what is elevated of the land.
And it has been read ﴿نُنْجِيكَ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
It is narrated from Yazīd al-Makkī that he read ﴿فاليَوْمَ نُنَحِّيك﴾ with ḥāʾ (We shall set you aside).
﴿بِبِدَنِكَ﴾: It was said: that is, alone. And it was said: with your coat of mail.
Mujāhid said: «بحسدك». And this is the best of the views. «[Translator's note: «بحسدك» (with your envy) is evidently a misprint for «بجسدك» (with your body), as the following sentence shows.]»
It was said: Its meaning is: with your body only, that is, naked, without a soul.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ مُبَوَّأَ صِدْقٍ﴾.
That is: We settled them.
Qatāda said: He means Syria and Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Egypt and Syria.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِن كُنتَ فِي شَكٍّ مِّمَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ فَاسْأَلِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقْرَءُونَ ٱلْكِتَابَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
There are several views on its meaning:
1- Among them: that the address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to his community; so the meaning on this [view] is:
"if you [plural] are in doubt", as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ﴾.
2- And it was said: This is as it is said: "If you are my father, then do such-and-such", while he is his father.
3- And it was said: «إنْ» here is in the sense of «ما» (negation), as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنِ الكَافِرُونَ إلاَّ فِي غُرُورٍ﴾; and the meaning is: you were not in doubt about what We sent down to you, so ask those who read the Book before you — a question for
increase [of certainty], as He, the Exalted, said, informing about Abraham: ﴿قَالَ بَلَى وَلَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾.
Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: The meaning is: O Muḥammad, say to the doubter: If you are in doubt, ask those who read the Book, that is, ask whoever has believed among the People of the Book, and he will inform you of the description of the Prophet ﷺ in his scripture.
Al-Ḥasan said: He neither asked nor doubted.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "Those who read the Book" — by them he means whoever believed among the People of the Book and was among the people of piety.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِمْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, those against whom the anger and wrath of Allah have become due because of their disobedience do not believe.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ كَانَتْ قَرْيَةٌ آمَنَتْ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَانُهَا إِلاَّ قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾.
Qatāda said: No people believed when they saw the punishment except the people of Jonah.
Someone else said: They did not see the punishment; they only saw its sign, so their repentance was accepted.
This was mentioned right after the story of Pharaoh because he believed when he saw the punishment, and that did not benefit him.
Qatāda said: The people of Jonah went out and separated the animals from their young, and remained supplicating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, so He turned to them in forgiveness.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِلاَّ قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾.
This, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is an exception not from the first [category].
Others besides them said: It is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because they are a community other than the communities from which they were excepted, and not of their kind or likeness, even though they were of the children of Adam.
The meaning of ﴿إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾ is: until the time their life-spans run out.

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ لآمَنَ مَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them: that it had preceded in His knowledge that none would believe except one for whom happiness had been decreed beforehand in the first record, as Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: "He, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed him that none would believe except one for whom happiness from Allah had been decreed beforehand in the first record, and none would go astray except one for whom wretchedness from Allah had been decreed beforehand
in the first record."
The other view: Had your Lord willed, He would have hastened punishment upon the disbeliever, and then all people would have believed; but had that been so, there would be no reward for them in believing; so the trial occurred according to wisdom.
And from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُ الرِّجْسَ﴾ — he said: wrath.
Then He said: ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾, that is, they do not understand from Allah His arguments, His admonitions and His proofs that point to prophethood.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿قُلِ ٱنظُرُواْ مَاذَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
[That is, of the evidence of the power of Allah, exalted be His mention.]
Then He said: ﴿وَمَا تُغْنِي ٱلآيَاتُ وَٱلنُّذُرُ﴾, that is, the proofs; and «النُّذُر» is the plural of «نذير», which is the messenger; ﴿عَن قَوْمٍ لاَّ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is, who do not believe until they see the punishment.

nahhas-meani:102-102.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَهَلْ يَنتَظِرُونَ إِلاَّ مِثْلَ أَيَّامِ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوْاْ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
He means these deniers, [awaiting] punishment.
﴿إِلاَّ مِثْلَ أَيَّامِ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوْاْ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He says: the [punitive] strikes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, against those who passed away before them — the people of Noah, ʿĀd and Thamūd.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي رُسُلَنَا وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾.
That is: from that destruction. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾: that is, as We did with those of the past.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِن كُنتُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِّن دِينِي﴾.
That is: [the religion] to which I call you, so that you do not know that it is the truth. ﴿فَلاَ أَعْبُدُ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — of idols and other things, which neither benefit in anything nor harm. ﴿وَلَـٰكِنْ أَعْبُدُ ٱللَّهَ﴾, about whom you ought not to doubt, ﴿ٱلَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ﴾, that is, who takes the souls of the creatures and causes them to die. ﴿وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: that is, and He has commanded me to be among those who believe.

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَنْ أَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفاً﴾.
The second «أنْ» is conjoined to the first; that is: set yourself firmly upon the religion of Islam. ﴿حَنِيفاً﴾: inclining to Islam. ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾: that is, of those who associate rivals in His worship.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَدْعُ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَنفَعُكَ وَلاَ يَضُرُّكَ﴾.
That is: neither in religion nor in worldly life.
﴿فَإِن فَعَلْتَ فَإِنَّكَ إِذاً مِّنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾: that is, if you did that and worshipped them, then you would be among those who wrong themselves.

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإِن يَمْسَسْكَ ٱللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ فَلاَ كَاشِفَ لَهُ إِلاَّ هُوَ﴾.
That is: not what these idolaters worship. ﴿وَإِن يُرِدْكَ بِخَيْرٍ﴾: that is, with ease and blessing, well-being and joy, ﴿فَلاَ رَآدَّ لِفَضْلِهِ﴾: that is, no one is able to come between you and that, nor to turn it away from you, because He is the one in whose hand that lies, not anyone else.

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ قَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ﴾.
That is: the Qurʾān, in which is the explanation of what people need. ﴿فَمَنُ ٱهْتَدَىٰ﴾: [whoever] follows the path of truth, ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَهْتَدِي لِنَفْسِهِ﴾: that is, he only keeps upright on guidance for his own good. ﴿وَمَن ضَلَّ﴾: that is, [whoever] turns away from the truth that has come to him, ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا﴾: that is, he only commits a wrong thereby against himself, not against anyone else.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَنَاْ عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ﴾.
That is: I have not been given authority to set you straight; your affair belongs only to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; He is the one who sets straight whom He wills among you, and I am only a conveyor [of the message].

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّبِعْ مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيْكَ﴾.
That is: act according to it.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَٱصْبِرْ﴾, that is, over what befalls you for the sake of Allah from the idolaters of your people, ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَحْكُمَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, that is, until He passes judgement concerning them.
And it was said: His command [comes] with a decisive act. ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْحَاكِمِينَ﴾: that is, the best of judges and the most just of those who decide.
Ibn Zayd said: This is abrogated; Allah decreed fighting them and commanded harshness towards them.
Someone else said: He judged between him and them on the day of Badr, and killed them by the sword, and commanded His Prophet ﷺ, concerning those of them who remained, to take them along the path of those of them who had been destroyed, or [else] they repent.
